newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was sharply higher on light demand and light offerings early, USDA said.
Retail demand was again for their immediate needs, forward interest continued fairly light, as many retailers were searching for other protein items for new featuring needs.

Rib and loin cuts experienced the higher price gains as most retailers were caught short on unexpected good consumer demands. Chucks cuts were generally higher for the week, some chuck cuts continued to be stimulated by last week's improved export demand.

Round cuts also traded higher as these cuts continued to see fairly good demand for immediate shipment on fairly light offerings. Closely trimmed items traded sharply higher on all cuts, with the chuck cuts experiencing the higher gains.

Beef trimmings traded lower on fairly light demand early in the week with mostly moderate offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were higher on mostly moderate demand and offerings, with good interest continuing in the chuck grinds for fed cattle and blended grinds.

For the week Select and Choice rib primal 4.00 to 8.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 2.00 to 3.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 4.00 to 4.50 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 5.00 to 9.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 3.00 to 4.50 higher; Beef trimmings 3.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 2.00 to 5.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 4.55 at 108.56; 700/850 Up 4.24 at 109.01; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 3.17 at 101.70; 700/850 Up 3.25 at 101.56.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The lean boneless beef market continued an upward trend this week on light to moderate demand and offerings. However, as the week progressed. Prices began to weaken as fast food demand declined. The 65% lean boneless beef traded lower on light demand and moderate offerings.

Despite the strength in the boneless beef market, cow carcasses traded steady to weak on light to moderate demand and offerings. Cow cuts traded uneven, with heavy tenderloins and ribeye rolls trading weak to lower and light tenderloins moved sharply higher on good demand.

In addition, the 100% lean flats and eyes rebounded after last week's loses on moderate to good demand. Utility steady to weak and Cutter carcasses not established; 90% boneless beef 1.00-2.00 higher; 85% 1.00-2.00 higher; 75% generally 4.00 higher; 65% 1.00-2.00 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, July 31, 1997 was estimated at 83.05 per cwt., up .90 from a week ago Friday.
